articles.title: High Court Rules Against Hopwood DePree in Ownership Dispute Over Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: A High Court ruling has determined that Rochdale Council acted fairly in denying ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the original builders.
articles.content_html:
A High Court in Manchester has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to transfer ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the family that built the historic property in the 1420s. The ruling concluded a two-day trial that examined the council's termination of an exclusivity agreement to sell the Grade II-listed hall to Mr DePree.

Following the court's decision, Mr DePree expressed disappointment, stating that the outcome was a significant setback for both the community and heritage rescue groups across the UK. He indicated that his legal team is currently exploring further options regarding the case. Mr DePree emphasised the importance of monitoring the council's efforts to preserve and restore Hopwood Hall for public benefit.

Hopwood Hall, which is now part of Hopwood Hall College, has a long history, having been owned by the Hopwood family until 1922. After being sold in 1942, it served various purposes, including a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. The hall has since fallen into disrepair and was acquired by Rochdale Council, which remains its owner.

The ruling raises questions about the future of Hopwood Hall and its restoration. The council's plans for the property and any potential community involvement in its future remain to be seen as Mr DePree and his team consider their next steps.
